Axios PM
By Mike Allen · Sep 04, 2026

🕶️ We made it. Happy holiday weekend! Today's newsletter, edited by Herb Scribner, is 698 words, a 2½-min. read. Thanks to Sheryl Miller for copy editing.

🚨 Scoop: The Trump administration is working on a post-war Middle East strategy. Now in the early stages of drafting, the plan is intended to guide the U.S. approach in the Middle East after the Iran war ends, Axios' Barak Ravid reports.

👀 Situational awareness: President Trump will use the Qatari-gifted Boeing luxury jet for his upcoming trip to Ireland — the first time he's used the plane overseas since his July catering-container escape in Turkey, the N.Y. Times' Maggie Haberman scoops. (Gift link)

 
 
1 big thing: Costly summer send-off
 
Illustration: Aïda Amer/Axios. Stock: Getty Images

Summer's last hurrah will come with persistent pump pain and pricey burgers, Axios' Avery Lotz reports.

  • Gas prices are almost certain to remain north of $4 per gallon over Labor Day weekend — a busy travel period that coincides with the intensifying midterm election season.

⛽ Labor Day gas prices are slated to be the highest on record, with market tracking firm GasBuddy and AAA predicting they'll surpass the previous high set in 2012.

  • That's coming off a record-setting August, where the monthly national average of $4.07 trounced 2022's record, according to AAA data.

✈️ For travelers flying over the weekend, airfare is nearly 20% higher than last year, AAA says.

  • Still, TSA predicts there will be more than 17 million travelers at airports across the country between Thursday and Wednesday.

🍔 A pound of ground beef costs $6.89 on average in July, up 10% from the year prior.

  • Share this story.
 
 
2. 📈 Labor market boom
 
Data: Bureau of Labor Statistics. Chart: Courtenay Brown/Axios

A labor market that looked shaky just a month ago now appears on much firmer footing, Axios' Courtenay Brown writes.

  • U.S. employers added 162,000 jobs in August, while the unemployment rate held steady at 4.1%, according to Labor Department stats out today.

📊 By the numbers: Job gains were more than triple the 53,000 jobs that economists anticipated.

  • Revisions released today show that employers added 55,000 more jobs in June and July combined than previously estimated.

🎨 The big picture: The better-than-expected report is fresh evidence of the labor market's resilience, easing fears that a hiring slowdown had taken hold.

How a fourth-generation farm stays on track with ChatGPT
 
 

On her family’s seed farm, Rachael Sharp is digitizing decades of crop data, using ChatGPT to troubleshoot, plan and act faster. In a shrinking industry, speed and access to knowledge help keep the farm moving forward.

3. ⚡️ Catch me up
 
An LED sign welcomes U.S. service personnel in Pattaya City, Thailand, yesterday. Photo: Chalinee Thirasupa/Reuters
  1. 🚢 Vendors and travel agents swarmed crew members of the USS Abraham Lincoln, now deployed for a record 286 days, as they streamed into Thailand's seaside resort city of Pattaya during a port call that ends this weekend. Go deeper.
  2. 🏛️ A Massachusetts judge declared a mistrial in the Lindsay Clancy case after giving the defense extra time to make a last-minute appeal over the deadlocked jury. The defense argued one of the 12 jurors wouldn't budge due to a potential bias against mentally ill people. Get the latest.
  3. ☢️ A new watchdog report finds that Lori Chavez-DeRemer, President Trump's former labor secretary, drank on the job, misused government funds and oversaw a "toxic, intimidating and humiliating" environment, Axios' Avery Lotz reports.
  4. 🪖 U.S. military officials say they're turning off ad trackers on several devices over fears that commercially available location data has been used to target Americans in the Middle East, according to letters released today. Read the story ... Read the letters.
  5. 🏀 WNBA commissioner Cathy Engelbert will retire in December after leading the league for seven years, during a time of tremendous growth and widespread controversy. See the announcement.
 
 
4. 🏈 1 for the road: Ready for some football?
 

Colorado's Boo Carter blocks Georgia Tech kicker Aidan Birr's field goal attempt to secure a 14-13 win yesterday in Atlanta. Photo: Kevin C. Cox/Getty Images
 

No matter where you are this Labor Day weekend, there's a good chance college football will be on the TV.

  • After last week's teaser, the CFB season will have its first full Saturday slate this weekend, kicking off the season in earnest.

🏈 Standout matchups include:

  • No. 7 Miami at Stanford (tonight, 9 p.m. ET, ESPN).
  • Clemson at No. 11 LSU (Saturday, 7:30 p.m. ET, ABC).
  • No. 9 Ole Miss vs. No. 24 Louisville (Sunday, 7:30 p.m. ET, ABC).

🏁 Fun fact: Last year's national champion, Indiana, opens its repeat campaign against North Texas Saturday (noon ET, Fox).

☁️ Herb's thought bubble: I don't care what happens for the rest of the season. My alma mater, UMass Amherst, had its biggest win of the year against Rutgers last night. I'll be celebrating that until January.
